reasons.C: Plain, chatty short sentences with artless repetition and a mild deadpan irony ('some kind of a crook') come closest to the passage's loose, conversational, slightly awkward movement, though the repetition is laid on a little thick.
reasons.A: Has the period feel and the wry understatement, but its balanced semicolon clauses and polished epigrams ('It must be solvent') are more finished and aphoristic than the author's rambling, offhand sentences.
reasons.B: Smooth, even-length modern expository sentences with anachronistic diction ('upmarket') and a tidy summarising close; it lacks the passage's quirky syntax, confiding asides and ironic tone.
